tagline: A small town on the Sakae Krang River, next to the Huai Kha Khaeng World Heritage forest
introHtml: Uthai Thani is a small town right on the Sakae Krang River, where locals still live in riverside houseboats and raise fish in floating cages the way they have for generations. The town itself is easy to walk: there's a morning market, old temples, and Khao Sakae Krang, a hill you climb to pay respects and look out over the whole town. Head out toward Ban Rai and you reach Huai Kha Khaeng, a World Heritage wildlife sanctuary, and Hub Pa Tad, a sunken valley packed with pandanus and ancient ferns so dense the light comes through in beams. It's an unhurried province with few crowds, the kind of place you take slowly.
bestTime: November to February, when the weather is cool and comfortable for walking around town and climbing Khao Sakae Krang. Hub Pa Tad and the waterfalls around Ban Rai are at their greenest in late rainy season and early winter.

highlights.name: Sakae Krang River and houseboats
highlights.blurb: A small river running through town that still has houseboats and floating fish cages. Take a boat to see riverside life, or just walk the bank in the evening.

highlights.name: Khao Sakae Krang and Wat Sangkat Rattana Khiri
highlights.blurb: A low hill in the middle of town. Climb the Naga staircase or drive up to pay respects and look out over all of Uthai. It's the town's signature viewpoint.

highlights.name: Wat Tha Sung (Wat Chantharam)
highlights.blurb: A large temple on the Sakae Krang River, with a Glass Hall covered in mirrors that everyone stops to see. Grand but still peaceful.

highlights.name: Huai Kha Khaeng
highlights.blurb: The Huai Kha Khaeng Wildlife Sanctuary, one of the most intact World Heritage forests in Thailand and home to tigers and rare wildlife.

highlights.name: Hub Pa Tad
highlights.blurb: A closed-in valley dense with pandanus and ancient ferns. Walking the trail through it feels like stepping into a prehistoric forest, with light coming down in beautiful shafts.

highlights.name: Morning market and Trok Rong Ya walking street
highlights.blurb: A riverside morning market where locals actually shop for food, plus the old-shophouse district of Trok Rong Ya, which becomes a walking street on weekends.

foodScene.name: River fish and grilled fish
foodScene.note: Being on the Sakae Krang, the town has fresh freshwater fish straight from the cages — grilled fish, fish tom yum, and fried fish at the riverside restaurants.

foodScene.name: Boat noodles and old noodle shops
foodScene.note: The town has several long-running noodle shops with well-rounded broth — an easy meal that locals here grew up on.

foodScene.name: Kuay jab yuan
foodScene.note: Rolled rice-sheet noodles in a clear broth topped with pepper. You'll find it in town — a breakfast dish locals love.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are everywhere in town and along the roadside — bold flavors that suit travelers.

foodScene.name: Moo kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with plenty of places to choose from. Relaxed atmosphere and friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Riverside and in-town cafes
foodScene.note: Along the Sakae Krang River and in the old town there are small cafes where you can sip coffee and watch the houseboats.

foodScene.name: Local sweets and souvenirs
foodScene.note: Traditional Thai sweets and local souvenirs are sold at the markets and shops in town to take home.

attractions.name: Khao Sakae Krang and Wat Sangkat Rattana Khiri
attractions.blurb: A hill in the middle of town. Climb the Naga staircase to pay respects and take in the view over all of Uthai, with a bell and a mondop housing the Buddha's footprint at the top.

attractions.name: Wat Tha Sung (Wat Chantharam)
attractions.blurb: A large temple on the Sakae Krang River with a Glass Hall covered entirely in mirrors — grand but peaceful, and a usual stop for anyone visiting Uthai.

attractions.name: Sakae Krang River and houseboats
attractions.blurb: The river through town still lined with houseboats and fish cages. Take a boat to see riverside life, or walk the bank in the evening.

attractions.name: Huai Kha Khaeng Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.blurb: One of the most intact World Heritage forests in Thailand, with a nature trail and the grave of Seub Nakhasathien.

attractions.name: Hub Pa Tad
attractions.blurb: A closed-in valley dense with pandanus and ancient ferns. Walking the trail through it feels like entering a prehistoric forest, with light coming down beautifully.

attractions.name: Khao Khong Chai cave and Pha Raet, Ban Rai
attractions.blurb: A cluster of limestone hills and caves in Ban Rai district, with viewpoints and hiking trails — good for nature lovers who want to get out of town.

attractions.name: Wat Ubosatharam (Wat Bot)
attractions.blurb: An old temple on the Sakae Krang River with early Rattanakosin-era murals and a floating ordination hall that's part of Uthai's identity.

attractions.name: Trok Rong Ya and the old town market
attractions.blurb: A district of old shophouses and wooden homes turned into a walking street, with food and cafes to wander on weekends.
